title: Movement
description: One resistance-training movement, described in the fields a program actually computes with. Facts only: no instructional prose copied from anywhere, no images.

id.description: Stable slug, derived from the canonical name at first publication. Never re-used, never changed — a renamed movement keeps its id and gains an alias.

name.description: The canonical gym name, equipment first where equipment distinguishes it ('Cable Lateral Raise', not 'Lateral Raise, Cable').

aliases.description: Other names the same movement answers to. These are what let an app resolve a coach's or athlete's wording to one record instead of forking a second.

pattern.description: Movement pattern. 'none' for isolation work that belongs to no pattern (curls, raises, extensions).

loadType.description: How it is loaded. Drives plate maths, rounding and what a room can actually do.

mechanic.description: Multi-joint or single-joint. Absent from every other open dataset we found.

primaryMuscle.description: The muscle the movement is for, in common anatomical English ('Latissimus Dorsi', 'Gluteus Maximus').

secondaryMuscles.description: Every muscle doing meaningful work besides the primary. A recovery model credits these at a fraction of the primary, so an empty list under-counts training.

unilateral.description: Trained one side at a time, so a prescribed load is per side and reps are per side.

strengthTracked.description: Whether an estimated one-rep max is meaningful for it. False for most isolation, carries, holds and jumps.

transfers.description: Like lifts whose strength carries over, closest relative first. This is what lets an app open an unfamiliar movement at a sensible weight instead of guessing.

reference.description: The canonical name of a more common movement.

ratio.description: this movement ≈ ratio × reference, at the same reps.

basis.description: Whether the ratio comes from published training standards or from well-established coaching practice.

equipmentNotes.description: What a room needs beyond the load type ('a rack with safeties', 'a bench set to 30-45°'). Short, factual, no coaching.

sources.description: What the research consulted when the record was authored. Provenance, not content: nothing here is quoted into the record.

reviewed.description: When a human last checked it. Null means machine-authored and unreviewed — treat the ratios with more suspicion than the muscles.
